 ATP Almaty Day 4 Predictions Including Daniil Medvedev vs Sho Shimabukuro 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 The ATP Almaty Open heats up as the final round of sixteen matches are set for day 4, and the path to the quarterfinals is lined with danger. Home hope Alexander Bublik faces a stern test from Fabian Marozsan, while top seed Daniil Medvedev launches his campaign against qualifier Sho Shimabukuro. With a place in the quarterfinals on the cards, who do you back to make the next round?
 ATP Almaty Day 4 Predictions
 Terence Atmane vs Mattia Bellucci
 Head-to-Head : Atmane 1-0 Bellucci
 Terence Atmane arrives in the ATP Almaty second round after beating Rinky Hijikata in straight sets, using his aggressive baseline game to take control after a tight opening set. Bellucci had a more demanding route, recovering from a second-set dip to defeat sixth seed Tomas Martin Etcheverry in three sets.
 Both players can generate considerable pace from the baseline, but Atmane’s willingness to take risks and dictate early could be important on the indoor hard courts. Bellucci is left-handed and can create awkward angles, and his victory over Etcheverry should give him confidence he can handle pressure in a close contest. Atmane’s cleaner opening-round win and previous success against the Italian give him a slight edge, although Bellucci has the tools to extend the match.
 Prediction: Atmane in 3 
 Tomas Machac vs Karen Khachanov
 Head-to-Head: Khachanov 1-0 Machac
 Tomas Machac and Karen Khachanov renew their rivalry after Khachanov beat Machac in the third round of the 2024 Australian Open in four sets. Machac has since established himself as a dangerous hard-court opponent, combining quick movement with the ability to redirect pace and take the ball early. He arrives after a comfortable straight-sets win over wildcard Zangar Nurlanuly, dropping just two games.
 Khachanov also looked sharp in his opener, defeating qualifier Rei Sakamoto in straight sets. His powerful serve and heavy groundstrokes make him difficult to contain when he finds his range, particularly on a fast indoor surface. Machac’s movement and ability to vary the pace could make this competitive, but Khachanov has the more imposing serve and a proven record in high-pressure matches. If he maintains the level he showed against Sakamoto, he should have enough to come through another demanding encounter.
 Prediction: Khachanov in 3 
 Alexander Bublik vs Fabian Marozsan
 Head-to-Head : First meeting
 Alexander Bublik begins his ATP Almaty campaign against Fabian Marozsan after receiving a first-round bye as the third seed. Playing at home gives the Kazakh an added incentive, and his unpredictable style can be especially effective indoors. A big serve, sudden changes of pace, and willingness to come forward allow him to disrupt opponents before they can settle into a rhythm.
 Marozsan has already shown that he can handle the conditions, defeating Timofey Skatov in straight sets to reach this stage. The Hungarian is a clean ball-striker who can redirect pace and find angles from both wings, making him a dangerous opponent if Bublik’s level fluctuates. However, Bublik’s serve should provide a reliable platform, while his variety can force Marozsan into uncomfortable positions. With the home crowd behind him and fresh legs after his bye, Bublik has the edge, though Marozsan’s timing could make this a tight contest.
 Prediction: Bublik in 3 
 Daniil Medvedev vs Sho Shimabukuro
 Head-to-Head : First meeting
 Daniil Medvedev starts his ATP Almaty campaign against Sho Shimabukuro after receiving a first-round bye. The top seed will be keen to make an immediate statement, and his return game should be a major asset against a qualifier making his way through a difficult draw. Medvedev’s ability to absorb pace, extend rallies and force opponents to hit extra shots makes him particularly tough to beat when he finds his rhythm on hard courts.
 Shimabukuro has earned this opportunity by defeating Roman Safiullin in three sets, showing composure after losing the opening set. The Japanese player will need to serve well and take his chances early, because allowing Medvedev to dictate from the baseline could leave him chasing points for much of the match. Shimabukuro’s recent win should give him confidence, but Medvedev’s experience at the highest level, defensive coverage, and consistency make him a formidable challenge. Unless the qualifier produces an exceptional serving performance, the top seed should progress in straight sets at ATP Almaty.
 Prediction: Medvedev in 2
